title: Accelerator lane for high-velocity enterprise asks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We currently treat all customer feature asks through a single intake path. Top accounts and strategic partners that require expedited evaluation, commitment windows, and clear SLOs are waiting multiple cycles for decisions. This causes churn in sales negotiations and confusion for customer success and engineering about scope and SLAs.

Proposal: Create an 'Accelerator Lane' — a curated, SLA-backed intake and commitment track for high-velocity enterprise asks. The lane provides a fast triage, a three-step readiness check (feasibility, product fit, infra risk), and a commitment window template (90/180/365 days) with clear fallbacks if commitments cannot be met. The lane coordinates PM, Engineering, Solutions, Sales, and Support with templated playbooks and a small cross-functional SWAT that can be spun up per request.

Goals:
- Reduce decision lead time for qualifying enterprise asks from ~8 weeks to <= 10 business days.
- Provide a predictable commitment model sales can reference during negotiations.
- Surface cost and risk trade-offs early (engineering level-of-effort, infra needs, SLO delta).
- Maintain roadmap integrity by routing high-effort asks into canary or paid-backlog lanes with clear commercial offsets.

Scope and guardrails:
- Qualification: must meet "Top Account or Strategic Partner" criteria; minimum ARR or strategic metrics.
- Commitment types: exploratory evaluation (no SLA), pilot commitment (timeboxed support, no firm roadmap commitment), delivery commitment (timeboxed delivery window with associated commercial terms).
- Fallbacks: if engineering capacity or infra constraints block delivery, automatic downgrade to pilot or prioritized backlog with communication templates.

Success metrics:
- Median intake decision time <= 10 business days for qualified requests.
- >80% sales satisfaction with commitment clarity in post-mortem surveys.
- No net increase in unplanned roadmap churn (track via weekly changelog diff).

Operational components to build:
1) Intake form and rubric (Console/Forms + internal intake dashboard).
2) SLA templates and commitment playbook (Confluence + email templates).
3) Routing rules in Linear/Console tags to create an "Accelerator" queue.
4) Telemetry: intake lead time, engineering LOE estimates, fallbacks, conversion to paid work.
5) Billing/Commercial model: pilot credits, prioritized delivery add-on.

Out of scope for Phase 1: automated billing integration, multi-region deployment guarantees, and full legal contract changes (these will be handled by Sales/Legal as necessary).
acceptance_criteria: A published intake rubric and form for qualifying requests exists and is accessible to Sales and CS (link in attachments)
Routing rule in Linear that tags qualifying tickets as 'accelerator' and routes to a dedicated PM queue is implemented
SLA/commitment templates (exploratory/pilot/delivery) drafted and approved by Sales and Legal
Dashboard shows lead time from submission to decision and is populated with initial pilot data
Operational playbook with fallbacks and communication templates published and tested in one live customer case
comments: 2026-03-02 - Marcus Liu: Initial scoping review with Eng infra team. Major risk is autoscale predictability for Dedicated customers if we promise delivery windows without capacity reservations. Suggested mitigation: include capacity reservation options as part of the commercial commitment.
2026-03-04 - Priya Kapoor (Sales): Sales validated the rubric with two AE leads; they want a 'soft-yes' pilot path they can offer immediately while delivery evaluation is underway.

2026-03-06 - Elena Gomez (Legal): Legal flagged that 'delivery commitment' language must reference engineering SLOs and explicit acceptance criteria in the contract addendum. We'll need template language before pilots convert to delivery commitments.
2026-03-09 - Marcus Liu: POC linear routing rule created (see attachment). Requires ENG-8009 change to add 'accelerator' priority queue when ticket has label 'top-account' + 'escalation'.
2026-03-11 - Aisha Patel: Runbook drafted, uploaded to Confluence; next step is a shadow run with one active customer next week to validate decision timelines. Assigned to Marcus for orchestration.
decision_log: 2026-03-05 - Decision to limit Accelerator lane to Top Accounts & Strategic Partners only (to avoid emptying engineering capacity).
2026-03-07 - Decided on three commitment tiers (Exploratory, Pilot, Delivery) with explicit fallback messaging agreed by PM/Sales/Legal.
2026-03-10 - Agreed to require Sales to include a commercial credit or accelerated delivery fee for Delivery commitments to offset roadmap displacement.
notes: Potential follow-ups: integrate with Dedicated capacity reservation UI (ENG-11234) and surface cost implications in the Console cost breakdown.
Consider a small accelerator budget from GTM for initial pilots to reduce sales blocker friction.
We should track both attempted and successful accelerator conversions to measure ROI on engineering prioritization.
